SqueakyCleanText is a text-processing pipeline for training and RAG datasets.

Language detection, text repair, PII handling, scoring and data cards.

I benchmarked its PII stage alongside other tools: 18 entries, 12 datasets. Tested SCT version: v0.8.2.

The PII stage also acts as a router.

SCT has its own regex detection and language-based model routing. You can choose supported backends and models: ONNX, PyTorch, GLiNER, or Presidio/GLiNER.

The pipeline is not tied to one detection model.

On shared emails, phones and numbers, four tools have higher masking recall than SCT default: PII-Tracer, BardsAI-v3, OPF and OpenMed.

These are synthetic-data, matched-document comparisons. The image shows every pair whose 95% interval favours the other tool.

Across the broader label set, SCT default has higher recall in 13 of 14 paired synthetic comparisons. The GLiNER2-Fastino interval crosses zero.

Unsupported types count as misses, so this also measures entity coverage. Intervals are unadjusted.

One example: PII-Tracer has higher masking precision than SCT on the same synthetic data, 78.1% vs 75.0%. These are dataset averages.

Precision counts predicted mask spans that overlap a labelled mention. It is a separate measure from recall.

In that same pair, SCT has higher recall, but its document-exposure rate is higher: 58.0% vs 50.2%, averaged across datasets.

Recall counts any overlap. A partly masked identifier can still leave sensitive letters or digits visible.

This benchmark tests PII configurations, not the whole processing pipeline.

It tested v0.8.2. v0.8.3 is available, but these results do not measure it.
